Executive decision brief

WhatsApp transactional messaging is in incident state.

login_success and registration_success stopped delivering after 24 Apr 2026. The evidence points to sender phone-number registration, with a separate payload bug that must be fixed after recovery.

The story in one paragraph

Not a normal deliverability dip. A hard sender-state break.

Before 24 Apr, the sender had mixed problems: payload bugs, quality throttling, and some undeliverables. From 24 Apr onward, all sends failed with the same sender-side error. That pattern means product should treat WhatsApp as unavailable for login and registration confirmations until registration is restored.

0.0% success
Operating plan

Do these in order

  1. Stop new WhatsApp sendsPrevents guaranteed failures and quality damage.
  2. Turn on fallback channelProtects login/registration flow while WhatsApp is degraded.
  3. Re-register sender numberLiteral fix for 133010; needs MSG91/Meta path.
  4. Fix template payload bugEmpty components / wrong params caused 293 earlier failures.

27Other findings
281. Both templates underperform — even before the WABA broke. login_success delivered 18% (284 of 1,577); registration_success delivered 1/6 (only 6 ever sent).
302. The second-biggest failure mode is preventable: 'Template param mismatch' fired 293 times — 23% of all failures. The API is sending the user_name parameter in named-parameter format ({body_user_name: ...}) but the template was registered with a positional parameter slot. Engineering fix.
323. Meta-side quality throttling (131049) hit 252 times, mostly during the 27-29 March bulk-send burst. This is a sign that even before the registration broke, sender quality was degrading.
344. Read rate is alarming: only 15/285 delivered messages were marked as read (5.3%). For an OTP / login confirmation template, this should be >70%. Either users aren't opening WhatsApp, or read receipts are off, or the template is going to a stale list.
365. Registration_success has only been used 6 times — it appears to be a brand-new template that the team tried to launch right when the WABA went into 'review' state. The 29-Apr email to Meta confirms this.

Clean escalation summary

One sentence for leadership

Perccent sent 1,583 WhatsApp transactional messages; 1,295 failed, and from 24 Apr onward all 708 sends failed with sender deregistration error 133010, impacting 708 unique customers with zero WhatsApp confirmations.

Audit + deep research

Source-backed inputs to strengthen the report

This addendum combines the CSV audit with Meta/WhatsApp documentation references and operational guardrails. Items marked Official-linked use official Meta URLs plus rendered snippets/partner documentation where Meta pages were JS-heavy.

Audit verdict The report is directionally right; add recovery controls, source links, and escalation evidence.
Findings

Audit findings

Highest-impact gaps and corrective inputs.

P0MSG91 + Engineering

Sender registration is the active incident

From 24 Apr onward, 708 of 708 sends failed with 133010. This is a sender-side state issue, not a recipient-list quality issue.

Register the phone number through Meta/Cloud API path, then prove delivery with controlled test sends.
P0Product + Engineering

Transactional fallback is required

708 unique post-inflection customers were not reached by WhatsApp. Product should not wait for WhatsApp recovery before protecting login and registration confirmations.

Route OTP/login/registration confirmations to SMS or email while WhatsApp is degraded.
P1Engineering

Template payload bug predates the incident

293 failures came from a missing/incorrect body parameter pattern. CSV evidence shows empty components or alternate parameter keys on affected rows.

Align the live template parameter format with the send payload; add a pre-send contract test.
P1Product + Compliance

Marketing category is risky for login flows

The workbook notes login_success is registered as Marketing. Marketing templates can hit per-user limits and quality throttles; login confirmations should be reviewed for Authentication or Utility eligibility.

Do not relabel incorrectly, but submit the right category for the actual transactional use case.
P1Engineering + MSG91

Export lacks enough Meta-side debugging fields

MSG91 Request Id is present, but many failed rows have UUID undefined and no Meta trace/correlation fields. Escalation quality improves if every failure keeps the Meta error object.

Capture code, title, details, fbtrace_id, request id, phone_number_id, WABA ID, and timestamp in future exports.

Controls

Recommended monitoring guardrails

These thresholds are operational recommendations inferred from this incident pattern, not Meta-mandated limits.

Circuit breakerTrip on 10 consecutive 133010s

Also trip if last 25 WhatsApp sends fail above 80%. These are recommended thresholds based on this incident pattern.

Retry policyNever retry 133010 to users

Fix sender registration first. For 131049, use increasing backoff; for 131026, suppress noisy retry loops.

Delivery SLO90% delivered in 15 minutes

Historic delivered rows had p50 2s and p90 5m 43s; long-tail rows should be investigated separately.

Read healthRead tracking needs product review

Read p50 was 43m 22s across only 15 read receipts. Content/timing remains a separate problem after recovery.

Sources

Research sources used

Primary Meta sources are preferred. Partner docs are used only where they point back to official Meta pages or clarify returned error behavior.

Official

Meta registration endpoint

Phone-number registration uses POST /{Phone-Number-ID}/register with messaging_product=whatsapp and a 6-digit PIN.

Official

Meta Cloud API registration

Registration requests are capped at 10 per business number in a 72-hour moving window; exceeding this triggers a registration cooldown.

Official

Meta template message structure

Template sends with body variables require template components and parameter values that match the approved template.

Official-linked

Meta per-user marketing template limits

Meta limits marketing template delivery per user to protect user experience; 131049 aligns with this class of block.

Official-linked

Meta error-code page

Referenced by returned error payloads and partner docs for 131026/131049 handling.

Payload contract

Template send shape evidence

The CSV proves a separate payload contract issue. Fix it after registration recovery so the WABA does not return to the older 23% payload-failure baseline.

Bad pattern observed

Empty components

{
  "to": "918800000320",
  "type": "template",
  "template": {
    "name": "login_success",
    "language": {
      "code": "en",
      "policy": "deterministic"
    },
    "components": []
  },
  "messaging_product": "whatsapp"
}

Fails when approved template expects one body parameter.

Common pattern observed

Named wrapper

{
  "body_user_name": {
    "type": "text",
    "parameter_name": "user_name",
    "text": "Investor"
  }
}

Can work only if BSP/template mapping expects this shape; it does not fix 133010.

Cloud API positional pattern

One body variable

{
  "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
  "to": "<customer_number>",
  "type": "template",
  "template": {
    "name": "login_success",
    "language": {
      "code": "en"
    },
    "components": [
      {
        "type": "body",
        "parameters": [
          {
            "type": "text",
            "text": "Investor"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

Use this shape for a positional template with one body variable, or align named parameters at template creation.

Sender deregistered (133010)714

Engineering + MSG91 + Meta

The Perccent sender number is not registered on the WhatsApp Business Platform. Per Meta documentation, this is a SENDER-side state issue, not a recipient-side one. Resolution requires re-registering the phone number via the Cloud API /register endpoint, which requires whatsapp_business_management permission and a 6-digit PIN.
Template param mismatch290

Engineering

Template defines 1 body parameter ({{user_name}}), but the API call is sending the parameter in named-parameter format under key "body_user_name" — and the live template at Meta is registered with positional parameters. WhatsApp sees zero positional params, hence "(0) does not match the expected number of params (1)".
Meta quality throttle (131049)250

Marketing + Engineering

Meta is throttling messages from this sender to maintain "healthy ecosystem engagement". Triggered when sender quality rating drops or recipients have low historical engagement with the business. Often a leading indicator that the sender is heading toward harder restrictions.
Meta undeliverable (131026)36

No action — suppress retry

Generic "could not deliver" — recipient may have an outdated WhatsApp app, account issue, or be in a region where delivery is restricted. Lower volume and usually transient.

8. WABA Incident Case Study

1WABA / sender-deregistration incident — case study
2Synthesized from the 29-Apr email to Meta, the call-prep brief, MSG91 logs, and this CSV
4The facts at a glance
5BusinessPerccent (Mutual Fund Distributor platform)
6WABA ID319158824608826
7Phone number+91 89518 93121
8PlatformMSG91 WhatsApp Channel (BSP)
9Active templates in datasetlogin_success (1,577 sends), registration_success (6 sends)
10Date range analysed21 Mar 2026 – 30 Apr 2026
11Inflection point24 Apr 2026 — every prior failure mode disappears, only 133010 remains
12Concurrent issue (per 29-Apr email)"Display name still in review" + "This WABA is not allowed to create or update templates"
13Possible trigger (per call brief)Number swap between Manoj and Ekta on the consumer WhatsApp app
16Timeline of events
17DateEvent
1821 Mar 2026First login_success messages logged. Day starts with 1 message; build-up to 149/day by 27 Mar.
1922 Mar 2026First "Template param mismatch" failure logged — engineering payload bug exists from day one.
2024 Mar 2026First Meta-side errors appear: 131049 quality throttle (2) and 131026 undeliverable (1).
2127 Mar 2026Volume spike: 149 sends. 75 quality-throttle failures in a single day — Meta is actively rate-limiting this sender.
2228 Mar 2026145 sends, 81 param-mismatch failures (peak day for that bug). Sender quality clearly degrading.
23Late March – mid AprilDaily volumes drop to 5-30 messages. Failures continue at ~70-80%, dominated by the param mismatch + quality throttle.
2421 Apr 2026Volume picks up again (73 sends).
2522 Apr 202639 sends, all old failure types still present.
2623 Apr 2026INFLECTION DAY: Last day with the "old" mix of failures. First 6 occurrences of "133010 Account not registered" appear, alongside the usual mix.
2724 Apr 202615 sends, ALL FAIL with 133010. Every other failure mode has disappeared. The phone number has entered a deregistered/restricted state.
2825 Apr 20262 sends, both fail with 133010.
2926 Apr 20264 sends, all fail with 133010.
3027 Apr 2026128 sends, all fail with 133010 (0% delivery). Likely an automated retry queue.
3128 Apr 2026182 sends, all fail with 133010. Around 5:09 PM, Perccent first writes to MSG91 reporting "templates cannot be created/updated".
3229 Apr 2026238 sends, all fail with 133010. Sagnik sends the formal email to Meta support: WABA ID, phone number, MSG91 platform, requesting urgent review of WABA-level restriction, partner permissions, account quality. Meta call brief drafted for Animesh.
3330 Apr 2026139 sends, all fail with 133010 (100% failure). Status as of last data point: still broken.
36Most likely cause — and what the alternatives are
37ProbabilityHypothesisWhy this fits — and what evidence points to it
38HIGHPRIMARY HYPOTHESIS — Number swap deregistered the sender on the APIOn the consumer WhatsApp app, only one device can be logged into a given phone number at a time. When Manoj logged out and Ekta logged into the marketing number, and Manoj then logged into the utility number (+91 89518 93121, the API-connected one), the consumer-app login almost certainly triggered a re-registration on the consumer WhatsApp Business app — which deregisters the number from the WhatsApp Business Platform / API. From that moment, every API send to that number returns 133010.

This matches the data exactly: 23 Apr is the inflection. It matches Meta documentation: 133010 = phone number not registered on Business Platform. It matches the support thread: MSG91 saying "this error is returned directly by Meta".
39MEDIUMSECONDARY HYPOTHESIS — Independent WABA-level restriction triggered by qualityIn the weeks before 24 Apr, the sender was already accumulating quality throttles (131049) and undeliverable errors (131026). Meta automatically applies harder restrictions when sender quality stays low — including blocking template creation/updates and effectively suspending the WABA. The two issues (number swap + quality erosion) may have arrived at the same answer from two directions.
40LOWTERTIARY HYPOTHESIS — Display-name review or business verification flagThe 29-Apr email notes the display name is still "in review". Until display-name review completes, certain template operations and platform actions remain restricted. If review went into a stuck state around 24 Apr, that alone could produce the symptoms — though it would not normally produce 133010 specifically.
41NEAR-ZEROLEAST LIKELY — Recipient-side problemDespite the literal text of "(#133010) Account not registered", the recipients are not the cause. 100% of sends after 24 Apr cannot all suddenly be to non-WhatsApp numbers when the previous weeks had a normal mix. The recipient pattern did not change; the sender state did.
Action plan

Three time horizons

Immediate, short-term, and structural actions extracted from the recommendations sheet.

IMMEDIATE = today. SHORT-TERM = this week. STRUCTURAL = this month and beyond.

IMMEDIATE — today (stop the bleeding)

#1P0

Re-register the phone number on the WhatsApp Cloud API

This is the literal fix for error 133010. Make a POST request to graph.facebook.com/v21.0/{PHONE_NUMBER_ID}/register with body {"messaging_product":"whatsapp","pin":"<6-digit PIN>"} using an access token that has whatsapp_business_management permission. MSG91 may need to do this on Perccent's behalf, or expose a "Re-register number" button. Do this BEFORE any further template work — nothing else will deliver until this is fixed.

MSG91 + Engineering
#2P0

Stop sending login_success and registration_success until the WABA is restored

Every send right now is a guaranteed 133010 failure. Continued sends will further degrade sender quality at Meta, making the WABA harder to restore. Pause the trigger queue, and add a circuit breaker that suspends sends when the last 50 messages are all failing.

Engineering
#3P0

Have a FALLBACK channel ready for OTP / login confirmation TODAY

login_success is a USER-FACING transactional message — users are right now not getting login confirmations. Switch the OTP/login channel to SMS (or email) immediately, even if temporarily, so the user-visible flow does not break. WhatsApp can be re-added once the WABA is restored.

Product + Engineering
#4P0

Get a Meta case ID in writing on the support call

Per the call brief — do not let the call end without (a) confirmation of whether the WABA is restricted, (b) the exact reason code, (c) who needs to act, (d) a written case ID. Without a case ID nothing is trackable.

Animesh / Sagnik
#5P0

Do NOT log into +91 89518 93121 on any consumer WhatsApp / WhatsApp Business app

Per the call brief's "Things not to do" list — repeated app logins on a number that is supposed to be on the API will keep deregistering it. Lock the device, change the SIM custody, document who can hold the SIM.

Operations

SHORT-TERM — this week (fix what was broken before the WABA broke)

#1P1

Fix the template parameter mismatch in login_success

293 messages (23% of all failures pre-24 Apr) failed because the API call sends the user_name parameter in named-parameter format ("body_user_name"...) but the live WhatsApp template at Meta expects positional parameters. Two paths: (a) update the template at Meta to use named parameters and re-submit for review, OR (b) change the API call to send positional params: {"body":[{"type":"text","text":"Investor"}]}. Option (b) is faster.

Engineering
#2P1

Add CI validation that template payloads match live template schema before any send

The param mismatch went undetected for 5+ weeks. Add a pre-flight check: load the template definition from Meta on each deploy, validate that the calling code's payload conforms. Fail the build if they diverge. This prevents the same class of bug.

Engineering
#3P1

Pre-validate recipient WhatsApp registration before sending login_success

Even after the WABA is restored, you will still hit some 133010-style failures for recipients whose numbers genuinely aren't on WhatsApp. Use the Cloud API contacts endpoint or maintain a "WhatsApp-active" flag in your CRM that's updated whenever a delivery succeeds. Skip non-active users and route them to SMS instead.

Engineering + CRM
#4P1

Investigate the Haptik vs MSG91 partner-access matrix in Meta Business Manager

Per Meta call brief Hypothesis B — verify Haptik has Full Control and MSG91 has Partial Control with template-management task included. If two partners are both holding control, Meta may have flagged this as a configuration anomaly. Document the current state, then align it.

Animesh + Manoj
#5P1

Document the SIM-custody policy and the API-vs-app boundary

Single most important lesson from this incident: the +91 89518 93121 SIM is an API SIM, not a chat SIM. Anyone logging into it on a phone may deregister it. Write a one-page policy: who holds the SIM, where it is stored, what to do if someone needs to "use" the marketing number. Communicate to the team.

Operations + Sagnik

STRUCTURAL — this month (prevent the next incident)

#1P2

Build a deliverability monitoring dashboard

The 24-Apr inflection took ~4 days to reach the team's notice. A simple "delivery rate over last 24h" alarm with threshold <50% would have caught this within hours. Wire MSG91 webhooks into your existing analytics, draw a per-template line chart, set up email/Slack alerts. The data is already there; only the dashboard is missing.

Data / Analytics
#2P2

Add a second WhatsApp number as hot-failover

Single-number dependency means a single deregistration event takes down 100% of WhatsApp delivery — exactly what is happening now. Register a second phone number on the same WABA. Configure your sender code to round-robin, OR to fail over when one number returns 133010. Cost: one extra number.

Engineering + Ops
#3P2

Migrate transactional / OTP messages off the WhatsApp marketing template type

login_success is currently registered as a "Marketing" template (visible in the screenshot). For OTP/transactional messages, register an Authentication template instead. Authentication templates are subject to different (looser) ecosystem-quality throttling — and would likely have avoided most of the 131049 errors in March.

Engineering + Marketing
#4P2

Build a "WhatsApp-active" flag on each user record

On every successful delivery, set user.whatsapp_active=true. On every 133010 (recipient-side) failure for a recipient, set false and timestamp. Skip non-active users on next campaign send. Updates the recipient list automatically over time.

Engineering + CRM
#5P3

Apply for a higher messaging tier with Meta

Pre-WABA-break, the sender was hitting quality throttle on volume bursts of just 100-150 messages/day. That's a low tier. Once the WABA is restored, work with MSG91 to apply for a tier upgrade — the application requires a clean quality history (so wait until you've had 30 clean days post-recovery).

BSP / Ops
#6P3

Document a runbook for "the WABA broke" scenarios

Take the call brief Sagnik wrote and convert it to a permanent runbook: who calls Meta, what to ask, what to NOT do (delete WABA, log into number, etc.), what fallback channels exist. Store it where the on-call team can find it. Practice it once in a fire-drill.

Sagnik + Engineering

Support call

Exact questions for Meta

Ordered by what the data now indicates.

Goal of the call

  1. Get a definitive answer to ONE question:
  2. Why is +91 89518 93121 returning error 133010 on every API send, and what is the exact action sequence
  3. to restore registration?
  4. Do not let the call end with 'check permissions'. Get specifics.

Phone-number registration state (lead with this — the data points here)

  1. 1. Confirm the WABA ID and Phone Number ID currently associated with +91 89518 93121.
  2. 2. Is this phone number CURRENTLY registered on the WhatsApp Business Platform? Yes or no — get a clear answer.
  3. 3. When did the registration state change? Specifically, was there any state change between 22-24 April 2026?
  4. 4. Did the recent login of this number on a consumer WhatsApp / WhatsApp Business app trigger a deregistration?
  5. 5. What is the exact sequence to re-register: who calls /register, with what permission, what PIN, what region setting?
  6. 6. Is there any cooldown (e.g. 5-minute or 72-hour rate-limit window) we need to wait through before re-registration?
  7. 7. Confirm that re-registering will not affect the WABA ID, business verification, display name, or template approvals.

WABA-level restriction

  1. 1. Is the WABA itself currently restricted — separately from the phone-number issue?
  2. 2. Does the WABA have an active restriction on creating/updating templates? When was it applied?
  3. 3. What is the exact internal reason code? "Display name in review" alone, or something else?
  4. 4. Was the WABA previously restored (per the email, this happened earlier)? When did the current restriction apply?
  5. 5. Will restoring the WABA also restore template create/update — or are these separate steps?

Partner access (Haptik + MSG91)

  1. 1. List all partners currently with access to WABA 319158824608826.
  2. 2. Does Haptik have Full Control as expected?
  3. 3. Does MSG91 have Partial Control with the specific template-management task included?
  4. 4. Which partner / app / system user does Meta SEE in the failed template-create / template-update API calls?
  5. 5. Can Meta confirm whether the 133010 errors are from MSG91's system user calls or from a different app?

Account quality / business verification

  1. 1. Is the Meta Business Portfolio fully verified and in good standing?
  2. 2. Is the WABA in good standing? Any hidden account-quality flags?
  3. 3. Are any policy / integrity / spam flags affecting marketing or utility template categories specifically?
  4. 4. Is the display-name review actually progressing, or is it stuck? Expected resolution time?

Resolution sequence

  1. 1. In what exact order should the following steps happen: re-register phone? restore WABA? re-share with MSG91?
  2. 2. What does Perccent need to do?
  3. 3. What does MSG91 need to do?
  4. 4. What, if anything, does Haptik need to do?
  5. 5. Get a written case ID before ending the call. Without it, the case cannot be tracked or escalated.

DO NOT do until Meta confirms

  1. ✗ Do not delete the WhatsApp Business Account from any device.
  2. ✗ Do not remove MSG91 or Haptik partner access randomly.
  3. ✗ Do not disconnect the number from the Business Platform.
  4. ✗ Do not retry template submissions repeatedly from multiple places — this can trip rate limits.
  5. ✗ Do not re-register or migrate the number without MSG91 / Meta confirming the correct sequence.
  6. ✗ Do not change business verification or ownership settings unless Meta explicitly asks.
  7. ✗ Do not log the number into a consumer WhatsApp / WhatsApp Business app under any circumstance.

Notes

Methodology and data notes

Definitions, categorization logic, caveats, and rebuild notes.

Data source

Single CSV export from MSG91 (WhatsApp BSP) covering the Perccent WABA. File: whatapp.csv. 1,583 rows, all outbound (Direction=1), all template messages.

Period covered

First message: 21 Mar 2026 13:22:34. Last message: 30 Apr 2026 14:21:56. 40 active days.

Templates

Only two templates appear in the data:
• login_success: 1,577 sends (99.6%) — the primary transactional/login template, registered as "Marketing" category in MSG91 (visible in the team's template editor screenshot).
• registration_success: 6 sends (0.4%) — appears to have been launched in late April, right around when the WABA went into restricted state. Only 1 of 6 successfully delivered.

Status definitions

WhatsApp messages move through: submitted → sent → delivered → read.
• "Delivered" in this report = delivery_report ∈ {delivered, read} — the message confirmably reached the recipient.
• "In flight" = delivery_report ∈ {sent, submitted} — message in transit at the time of export, final state unknown.
• "Failed" = delivery_report = "failed".
• "Read %" = read / delivered.

Failure categorization

Failure-reason strings were grouped into 4 categories based on Meta error codes:
• Sender deregistered (133010) — phone number not registered on WhatsApp Business Platform.
• Template param mismatch — "body: number of localizable_params (0) does not match the expected number of params (1)".
• Meta quality throttle (131049) — sender quality / ecosystem health throttling.
• Meta undeliverable (131026) — generic delivery failure.
These were rolled up into 3 root causes: WABA / sender registration, Engineering — payload bug, and Meta-side quality / restriction.

Inflection date

Throughout this report, 24 April 2026 is referred to as "the inflection". This is the first date on which (a) every message sent failed, AND (b) every failure carried error 133010 with no other failure modes appearing. The transition was sharp: 23 Apr had 6 occurrences of 133010 mixed with 8 param-mismatches, 5 quality-throttles, and 2 undeliverables; from 24 Apr onwards, no other failure mode has appeared in the data.

What error 133010 actually means

Per Meta's public WhatsApp Business Platform documentation: "Error 133010 / Account not registered — the phone number you are attempting to use has not been registered on the platform". This refers to the SENDER number, not the recipient. The literal recommended fix is to call the Cloud Graph API endpoint POST /{PHONE_NUMBER_ID}/register with messaging_product=whatsapp and a 6-digit PIN, using an access token with whatsapp_business_management permission. Source: Meta Cloud API documentation; corroborating walkthroughs at heltar.com and apps.make.com.

Cross-reference with the 29-Apr email and call brief

This report deliberately incorporates two separate documents the team supplied:
(a) Sagnik's 29-Apr email to Meta support describing "Display name still in review" and "This WABA is not allowed to create or update templates".
(b) The pre-call brief Sagnik prepared for Animesh, listing five hypotheses (WABA restriction, partner-access mismatch, system-user/API permission, phone-number registration, business verification).
The data in this CSV uniquely supports Hypothesis D (phone-number registration) as the proximate cause of the post-24-Apr failure pattern. The call brief's Hypotheses B, C, and E remain valid as parallel concerns that explain the WABA-level "templates not allowed to create/update" symptom — these are separate from but possibly correlated with the registration issue.

Caveats

1. A small number of messages may still have been in flight when the export ran — these show as "sent" rather than "delivered" or "failed".
2. The date range begins 21 Mar — before that, no login_success or registration_success messages were sent on this WABA (or are not in this export).
3. "Read %" is a lower bound — recipients may read messages later than the export time.
4. The MSG91 export does not include the Meta correlation/request ID for failed calls, which is what would be needed to ask Meta for the exact internal reason code per failure. Recommend adding this to future exports if MSG91 supports it.

Reproducibility

All summary tables in tabs 2-7 use Excel formulas referencing the count cells. To rebuild from a fresh export, replace tab "11. Raw Data" and re-run the categorization in Python (the FailCat and RootCause columns are computed by string-matching the Failure Reason field; logic is documented in the methodology above).

19Inflection date
20Throughout this report, 24 April 2026 is referred to as "the inflection". This is the first date on which (a) every message sent failed, AND (b) every failure carried error 133010 with no other failure modes appearing. The transition was sharp: 23 Apr had 6 occurrences of 133010 mixed with 8 param-mismatches, 5 quality-throttles, and 2 undeliverables; from 24 Apr onwards, no other failure mode has appeared in the data.
22What error 133010 actually means
23Per Meta's public WhatsApp Business Platform documentation: "Error 133010 / Account not registered — the phone number you are attempting to use has not been registered on the platform". This refers to the SENDER number, not the recipient. The literal recommended fix is to call the Cloud Graph API endpoint POST /{PHONE_NUMBER_ID}/register with messaging_product=whatsapp and a 6-digit PIN, using an access token with whatsapp_business_management permission. Source: Meta Cloud API documentation; corroborating walkthroughs at heltar.com and apps.make.com.
25Cross-reference with the 29-Apr email and call brief
26This report deliberately incorporates two separate documents the team supplied:
(a) Sagnik's 29-Apr email to Meta support describing "Display name still in review" and "This WABA is not allowed to create or update templates".
(b) The pre-call brief Sagnik prepared for Animesh, listing five hypotheses (WABA restriction, partner-access mismatch, system-user/API permission, phone-number registration, business verification).
The data in this CSV uniquely supports Hypothesis D (phone-number registration) as the proximate cause of the post-24-Apr failure pattern. The call brief's Hypotheses B, C, and E remain valid as parallel concerns that explain the WABA-level "templates not allowed to create/update" symptom — these are separate from but possibly correlated with the registration issue.
28Caveats
291. A small number of messages may still have been in flight when the export ran — these show as "sent" rather than "delivered" or "failed".
2. The date range begins 21 Mar — before that, no login_success or registration_success messages were sent on this WABA (or are not in this export).
3. "Read %" is a lower bound — recipients may read messages later than the export time.
4. The MSG91 export does not include the Meta correlation/request ID for failed calls, which is what would be needed to ask Meta for the exact internal reason code per failure. Recommend adding this to future exports if MSG91 supports it.
